newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes softer on swaps, long-bond rise.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes softer on swaps, long-bond rise.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed slightly weaker on Thursday on pre-weekend swaps and a rise in U.S. long-bond interest rates, traders said.
"The peso was under pressure from swaps and the long bond, but still traded within a narrow range," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 2.0 and 0.95 of a centavo weaker, respectively, at 7.8925/7.8970 and 7.8770/7.8820 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 1.8 centavos weaker at 7.8690/7.8730 per dollar.
Yields on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond stood at 6.50 percent, compared to a recent low of 6.32 percent.

Dealers often sell dollars in the same-day market to buy them back at 24 or 48-hour contracts prior to a weekend. These contracts do not need to be paid for until Monday, using pesos that may meanwhile be invested in the money market.
Dealers expected light trading on Friday, with a first support for the 48-hour peso at 7.90 per dollar, and a second support at 7.9250.
